chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Barqi from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hisham ibn Salim from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) would enter his home and say, 'Do you have something [to eat], or shall I fast?' If they had something, they would bring it to him, and if not, he would fast.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (title for Imam Ali)

ai.seo_question: What was Imam Ali's method for determining whether to fast or eat based on his family's provision?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights Imam Ali’s (AS) practical approach to fasting intention (*niyyah*), linking it directly to the availability of sustenance within the household. It underscores the Shia scholarly view that the physical capacity to fast, derived from having food, is intrinsically connected to the spiritual resolve, reflecting a holistic understanding of religious duty. This practice illustrates the Imam’s humility and his reliance on family provision as a means to fulfill the divine command.
